state.question: What lets the Tree of Thoughts approach back out of a dead end and try a different line of reasoning?
state.answer: In the Tree of Thoughts (ToT) framework, backing out of dead ends and switching to alternative reasoning paths is achieved by combining tree search algorithms with deliberate language model (LM) state evaluation [C1, C2, C6]:State Representation: ToT structures problem-solving as a tree where each node is an explicit partial solution state $s = [x, z_{1\dots i}]$, containing the initial input and the sequence of intermediate thoughts generated so far [C2].LM-Based Heuristic Evaluation: Rather than relying on rigid rules, the LM deliberately acts as a heuristic evaluator to assess states [C3, C4]. It can either evaluate states independently (generating scalar values or labels like "sure," "likely," or "impossible" via lookahead simulation and commonsense) or compare multiple alternative states in a prompt to vote for the best candidate [C4].Explicit Backtracking in DFS (ToT-DFS): When using depth-first search, the model explores a path until a terminal state is reached or the LM evaluator determines that solving the problem from the current state is impossible (i.e., its value falls at or below an acceptability threshold, $V \le v_{\text{th}}$) [C6]. When this occurs, the entire subtree beneath that node is pruned, and the algorithm backtracks directly to the parent state to explore the next candidate branch [C5, C6].Pruning and Path Selection in BFS (ToT-BFS): In breadth-first search, dead ends are abandoned across steps by evaluating all proposed continuation states and keeping only the top-$b$ most promising states for the next round, immediately filtering out unviable paths [C5, C6].

state.question: List the corpus papers whose titles mention debate, then give a short summary of what they argue.
state.answer:
The corpus contains two papers whose titles mention “debate”. [D1, D2]Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate — arXiv:2305.14325, published May 23, 2023. [D1]  
Argues that having language-model agents debate their answers improves factual correctness and reasoning accuracy. Agents can converge on more accurate answers, and the reported performance improves with more agents and debate rounds—though consensus is not necessarily correct. [C1, C2]ChatEval: Towards Better LLM-based Evaluators through Multi-Agent Debate — arXiv:2308.07201, published August 14, 2023. [D2]  
Argues that multiple LLM “referees” discussing text quality produce evaluations better aligned with human preferences than single-agent evaluators. It emphasizes diverse role prompts and communication strategies as key components of the approach, evaluated on open-ended question answering and dialogue-response benchmarks. [C6, C7, C8]

state.answer: MetaGPT assigns and structures roles for its agents through the following mechanisms:Explicit Role Profiles: Each agent is initialized with a specific profile defining its name, role profile, goals, constraints, specialized context, and operational skills (for example, allowing Product Managers to use web search tools and Engineers to execute code) while following ReAct-style behavior [C2].Standardized Operating Procedures (SOPs): MetaGPT models human software development workflows by encoding SOPs into prompt sequences and an assembly-line paradigm [C1]. This breaks complex tasks into sequential subtasks handled by five specialized roles: Product Manager (creates PRDs), Architect (system design and interface definitions), Project Manager (task allocation), Engineer (code implementation), and QA Engineer (testing and code quality verification) [C1, C2].Structured Deliverables: Rather than communicating via open-ended conversational dialogue, each role is constrained by schemas and formats to output structured deliverables—such as PRDs, interface definitions, and sequence flow diagrams—which serve as inputs for downstream roles [C2, C3].Publish-Subscribe Coordination: Agents coordinate asynchronously through a shared global message pool [C3]. Each agent monitors the pool and subscribes only to role-relevant prerequisite deliverables based on its profile (e.g., Architects subscribe to Product Manager PRDs), preventing information overload and triggering agent actions once all dependencies are met [C2, C3, C4].
